answer: A course I would genuinely love to take is one in creative writing, something I have long been curious about. I have always enjoyed writing, but I feel my skills are quite [[rudimentary]] and could benefit from proper guidance. I have a notebook full of half-finished short stories, mostly about village life and my grandparents' generation, but I never quite know how to shape them. I want to take it because writing well is such a valuable and [[versatile]] skill, useful in almost any field. In my job, for example, I often help students with their personal statements, and I can see how much a well-told story can strengthen an application. I would probably take it online, so I could fit it around my work, though a face-to-face class with feedback would be ideal. There are occasional workshops in Dhaka, so I might try to attend one when I visit my elder sister. What appeals to me most is the chance to learn techniques from experienced writers and to receive [[constructive criticism]]. Honestly, I think a good course could help me express my ideas far more clearly and creatively. It would also give me a productive and [[fulfilling]] hobby outside of work. I believe learning should be a lifelong pursuit, and this is one course I am determined to take eventually. It is exactly the kind of skill that could enrich both my professional and personal life, and who knows, perhaps one day I will finally finish one of those stories and see it [[in print]].

followUps.q: Would you write in English or Bengali?
followUps.answer: Probably both. Bengali feels more natural for stories about village life, because some expressions simply don't translate. But writing in English would help my work and reach a wider audience.

followUps.q: Have you ever shown your writing to anyone?
followUps.answer: Only to my younger sister, who is a very honest critic. She once told me a story was far too long and rather [[repetitive]], which hurt a little, but she was absolutely right.
